newsitem.title: MONTSERRAT: Volcano-plagued British colony seats government.
newsitem.headline: Volcano-plagued British colony seats government.

text.p: A coalition government headed by businessman Bertrand Osborne, was sworn in on Wednesday on the tiny British colony of Montserrat, plagued for over a year by an active volcano.

A brief statement from Government House said the government was made up of new chief minister Osborne, of the Movement for National Reconstruction (MNR), former Chief Minister Reuben Meade, Adelina Tuitt of the MNR and Rupert Weekes, an Independent candidate.

The new chief minister will have responsibility for finance and economic development, while Tuitt will be responsible for education, health and community services. Meade, who had been criticized for the government's handling of the long volcano crisis, is now Minister of Agriculture, Trade and the Environment. Weeks has been given the portfolio of communications and works, the statement said.

Chief Minister Osborne told the Caribbean News Agency that it was not "too difficult" to put the coalition government together. "So far, we have been doing very well. I think we are very close in this respect, I think we admire each other."

Life on Montserrat, a tiny island in the eastern Caribbean, has been difficult since its Soufriere Hills volcano roared to life in July 1995. Half of the island has been evacuated for much of the past 14 months.
